The 2026 NCAA Men's Final Four will be held at Lucas Oil Stadium with the National Semifinals being played on April 4 and the National Championship tipping off April 6. 2026 NCAA Final Four in Indianapolis The NCAA Men's Final Four is returning to Indianapolis. The city is no stranger to college basketball as the city has hosted 8 previous NCAA Final Fours in 1980, 1991, 1997, 2000, 2006, 2010, 2015, and 2021. History of the NCAA Men's Final Four The first college basketball tournament in America was decided on March 27, 1939 in Evanston, Illinois, the birthplace of tournament style basketball championships. The field of 8 drew a crowd of 15,000 over the course of the 10 day tournament. Today’s NCAA March Madness begins with a field of 68 and ends with the NCAA Final Four over a course of 18 days. Since its inception the tournament has seen 35 different champions. There are teams that win our hearts like John Wooden’s 10 time champion UCLA Bruins and teams that capture our imagination like the 1947 Holy Cross Crusaders winning it all, despite being the last seed. We even had the college basketball version of the Kentucky Derby in '12 when the rival Louisville Cardinals and Kentucky Wildcats faced off in the semifinals. The world is now in love with March Madness as the Men's Final Four draws crowds of 150,000 and is the most exciting weekend in all of sports. The 2026 NCAA Men's Final Four will be played at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN with the National Semifinals being played April 4 and the National Championship tipping off on April 6. The iconic stadium seats over 70,000, is the home of the Indianapolis Colts, and hosted a Super Bowl in 2012. Future Men's Final Four Locations Following the 2026 Men's Final Four in Indianapolis, the championship will then be held in Detroit in 2027 before being added to an always packed Las Vegas sports schedule for 2028.
